say: You give it a **histogram**. It tells you the shape, the centre and the spread, in words about the real situation.
The key idea: the height of each bar is how many values fall in that class, so look at where the bars pile up. Two separate peaks mean two groups.

example.question:
The histogram shows the time, in minutes, that 60 students spent on homework one night. The classes and the number of students in each are: 0–20: 5; 20–40: 22; 40–60: 8; 60–80: 4; 80–100: 21.
(i) Describe the shape of the histogram.
(ii) Estimate the mean.
(iii) What does the histogram tell you about the students?

steps.title: Read the shape
steps.say: Look for where the bars are tallest. Name each peak and say how many students it holds.

lines.text: The bars between the peaks are short. The shape is **bimodal**: it has two peaks.

steps.title: Find the mean
steps.say: Use the middle of each class as its value. Multiply by the number of students, add, and divide by the total.

steps.title: Check the mean against the bars
steps.say: A mean is only an average. Check how many students are really near it.

lines.text: The mean $\hl{1}{54.7}$ minutes is in the class 40–60.
Only 8 of the 60 students are in that class.

steps.title: Write the conclusion
steps.say: Say what the shape means for the students, in the words of the question.

lines.text: There are two groups: students who worked for about half an hour and students who worked for about an hour and a half. Hardly any student worked for the mean time of $\hl{1}{54.7}$ minutes, so the mean hides the two groups.

say: You give it the results of an analysis, such as a sample percentage and its margin of error. It writes a **conclusion** that answers the question that was asked.
The key idea: a sample only estimates the whole group, so the answer must allow for the margin of error and be written in the words of the question.

how.ordinary: Ordinary level only. It came up once, in 2021 Paper 2 Q7(b)(iii) (5 marks): after the interval is found, you state the conclusion in the words of the question.

example.question:
A survey of 400 adults found that 54% support a new bike lane. A councillor says: "The survey proves that more than half of all adults support the bike lane."
Find the margin of error and a 95% confidence interval for the percentage of all adults who support the bike lane. Is the councillor right?

steps.title: Find the margin of error
steps.say: The sample is only 400 adults, so the result is not exact. Find the margin of error, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$.

steps.title: Build the interval
steps.say: The true percentage lies within the margin of error of the sample percentage. Subtract it, then add it.

steps.title: Compare with the claim
steps.say: The councillor says $p$ is more than $50\%$. Ask: is $50\%$ inside the interval?

lines.text: $50$ lies between $\hl{2}{49}$ and $\hl{2}{59}$, so it is **inside** the interval.
So the true percentage could be $50\%$ or less.

steps.title: Answer in context
steps.say: Write the conclusion in the words of the question, not just "yes" or "no".

lines.text: No. The survey does not prove that more than half of all adults support the bike lane. The true percentage could be anywhere from 49% to 59%, and that includes 50% or less.

workedSolution.finalAnswer: \hl{2}{49}\% \le p \le \hl{2}{59}\%, \text{ so the claim is not proved}

ordinary.tip: Give the conclusion in the words of the question. A correct conclusion that is not in context loses marks.

sources.quote: Conclusion (from correct work) not in context

ordinary.tip: Write down $H_0$, $H_1$ and the interval, even if you are unsure of the rest. Any one of them earns marks.

sources.quote: Any one of H0 , H1, or Confidence

say: You give it a **claim**, such as "$45\%$ of customers buy popcorn". It writes two hypotheses: $H_0$ says the claim is still true and $H_1$ says it has changed.
The key idea: you test $H_0$. The data give enough evidence to **reject** it, or they do not. Either way you say what it means for the claim.

how.higher: Higher level, Paper 2: a step inside a longer hypothesis-test part in most years from 2015 to 2024. The hypotheses are the first of four steps marked (2022 Q5(b), 15 marks).
how.ordinary: Ordinary level, Paper 2, 2017 to 2022: a step inside the confidence-interval question. You write $H_0$ and $H_1$, then the conclusion and reason (2022 Q10(b)(iv), 10 marks).

example.question:
A cinema says that 45% of its customers buy popcorn. In a random sample of 625 customers, 250 bought popcorn.
Write down $H_0$ and $H_1$. Use the margin of error to test the cinema's claim and state your conclusion.

steps.title: Write the hypotheses
steps.say: $H_0$ is the claim as it stands. $H_1$ says the claim is wrong.

steps.title: Find the interval
steps.say: To test the claim, build the interval $\hat{p} \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ from the sample.

steps.title: Compare with the claim
steps.say: Is the claimed $45\%$ inside the interval?

lines.text: $45$ is bigger than $\hl{3}{44}$, so it is **outside** the interval.

steps.title: State the conclusion
steps.say: Outside the interval, so reject $H_0$. Say what that means for the claim.

lines.text: Reject $\hl{1}{H_0}$. There is evidence that the percentage of customers who buy popcorn is not $45\%$.
If $45\%$ had been inside the interval, you would not reject $\hl{1}{H_0}$. There would be no evidence against the claim.

higher.tip: Four steps are marked: hypotheses, calculations, conclusion, reason. Write all four.
Without a confidence interval or a test statistic you cannot earn the conclusion. Always show the calculation first.
Your reason must match your calculations. Say where the claimed value sits against the interval or the critical value.
Stating only the null and alternative hypotheses earns partial credit, so write them even if the calculation goes wrong.

ordinary.tip: Back the conclusion with the interval: say the claimed figure is outside it (or inside it).

sources.quote: The figure 65% is outside the 95% C.I.

ordinary.tip: Reject $H_0$ and say what has changed, in the words of the question.

sources.quote: Reject the Null hypothesis and conclude

ordinary.tip: Write the claimed value against the interval: "not within" the interval is the reason for rejecting.

sources.quote: 80% is not within the 95% C.I. above

ordinary.tip: Any one of $H_0$, $H_1$ or the interval written correctly earns marks.

sources.quote: Any one of H0 , H1, or Confidence

say: You give it a claimed percentage, a sample percentage $\hat{p}$ and the sample size $n$. It builds the interval $\hat{p} \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ and checks whether the claim is **inside** it.
The key idea: if the claimed value is inside the interval, the sample gives no evidence against it, so you do not reject $H_0$. If it is outside, you reject $H_0$.
what.out: interval; reject or do not reject

how.higher: Higher level, Paper 2: the interval step inside a hypothesis-test part, in 2023 and 2024 (2024 Q7(d), 10 marks, used $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ for a proportion).
how.ordinary: Ordinary level, Paper 2, every year 2017 to 2025. It is the last step of a statistics question: margin of error (5 marks), interval (5 marks), then the test of a claim (5 or 10 marks).

example.question:
A company says that 45% of its customers are under 30. In a random sample of 400 customers, 164 were under 30.
State $H_0$ and $H_1$. Find the margin of error and a 95% confidence interval. Test the company's claim and state your conclusion.

steps.title: Write the hypotheses
steps.say: $H_0$ is the company's claim. $H_1$ says the percentage is different.

steps.title: Find the margin of error
steps.say: First the sample percentage, then the margin of error $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$.

steps.title: Build the interval
steps.say: Subtract the margin of error from $\hat{p}$, then add it.

steps.title: Test the claim
steps.say: Is $45\%$ inside the interval? If it is, do not reject $H_0$.

lines.text: $45$ lies between $\hl{3}{36}$ and $\hl{3}{46}$, so it is **inside** the interval.
Do not reject $H_0$. There is not enough evidence to say that the percentage of customers under 30 is different from 45%.

workedSolution.finalAnswer: \hl{3}{36}\% \le p \le \hl{3}{46}\%, \text{ so do not reject } H_0

higher.tip: Show the interval or test statistic before you conclude. Without one, no conclusion can be drawn.
The reason must come from your calculation. The mark is for saying the claimed value is within or outside the interval.

sources.quote: must be based on relevant calculations

ordinary.tip: Round the margin of error properly. Giving no rounding, or the wrong rounding, costs a mark.

sources.quote: Apply a * for no or incorrect rounding

ordinary.tip: Work out both ends of the interval. One end alone is only partial credit.
Give the reason as "inside the range found" or "outside" it, and state the conclusion too.
A rejection is backed by the claimed value being outside the interval.

sources.quote: The figure 65% is outside the 95% C.I.
